subject: Inconsistent mean and sd in CMR models from JAGS compared to winbugs and nimble

messages.author: b402e24f27459c0e
messages.subject: Inconsistent mean and sd in CMR models from JAGS compared to winbugs and nimble
parts:
I compared the results of a simple Capture-mark-recapture model using an m-array from Jags, Winbugs and nimble.
Surprisingly, Jags gave different mean results and wider sd than nimble and Winbugs which gave similar results.
The 95% credible interval sin JAGS are thus very large. For instance for the probability of recapture:
  jags gave 0.20-0.93 compared to the others program: 0.53-0.64. The conclusions from JAGS can thus be really different form the other program.
Would anyone have an idea about the causes of these differences?
  Thanks
Floriane

Reproducible example:


# Capture-recapture data (in m-array format, from years 1 to 10)
m <- matrix(c(11,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  70,
              0, 12,  0,  1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  52,
              0,  0, 15,  5,  1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  42,
              0,  0,  0,  8,  3,  0,  0,  0,  0,  51,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  4,  3,  0,  0,  0,  61,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 12,  2,  3,  0,  66,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 16,  5,  0,  44,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 12,  0,  46,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 11,  71,
              10,  2,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  13,
              0,  7,  0,  1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  27,
              0,  0, 13,  2,  1,  1,  0,  0,  0,  14,
              0,  0,  0, 12,  2,  0,  0,  0,  0,  20,
              0,  0,  0,  0, 10,  2,  0,  0,  0,  21,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 11,  2,  1,  1,  14,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 12,  0,  0,  18,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 11,  1,  21,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 10,  26), ncol = 10, byrow = TRUE)


sink("ipmn.jags")
cat("
    model {
    # Survival and recapture probabilities, as well as productivity
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    sjuv[t] <- mean.sjuv
    sad[t] <- mean.sad
    p[t] <- mean.p
    }
   
    mean.sjuv ~ dunif(0, 1)
    mean.sad ~ dunif(0, 1)
    mean.p ~ dunif(0, 1)
   
    # 3.2 Likelihood for capture-recapture data: CJS model (2 age classes)
    # Multinomial likelihood
    for (t in 1:2*(nyears-1)){
    m[t,1:nyears] ~ dmulti(pr[t,1:nyears], r[t])
    }
   
    # m-array cell probabilities for juveniles
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    # Main diagonal
    q[t] <- 1-p[t]
    pr[t,t] <- sjuv[t] * p[t]
    # Above main diagonal
    for (j in (t+1):(nyears-1)){
    pr[t,j] <- sjuv[t]*prod(sad[(t+1):j])*prod(q[t:(j-1)])*p[j]
    } #j   
    # Below main diagonal
    for (j in 1:(t-1)){
    pr[t,j] <- 0
    } #j
    # Last column: probability of non-recapture
    pr[t,nyears] <- 1-sum(pr[t,1:(nyears-1)])
    } #t
   
    # m-array cell probabilities for adults
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    # Main diagonal
    pr[t+nyears-1,t] <- sad[t] * p[t]
    # Above main diagonal
    for (j in (t+1):(nyears-1)){
    pr[t+nyears-1,j] <- prod(sad[t:j])*prod(q[t:(j-1)])*p[j]
    } #j
    # Below main diagonal
    for (j in 1:(t-1)){
    pr[t+nyears-1,j] <- 0
    } #j
    # Last column
    pr[t+nyears-1,nyears] <- 1 - sum(pr[t+nyears-1,1:(nyears-1)])
    } #t
   
    }
    ",fill = TRUE)
sink()

jags.data <- list(m = m, nyears = dim(m)[2], r = rowSums(m))
inits <- list(mean.sjuv = 0.5, mean.sad = 0.5, mean.p = 0.5)
parameters <- c("mean.sjuv", "mean.sad", "mean.p")
library(jagsUI)
ipm <- jags(jags.data, inits, parameters, "ipmn.jags", n.chains = 3, n.thin = 6, n.iter = 2000, n.burnin = 500)
print(ipm, digits = 3)
# mean    sd  2.5%   50%  97.5% overlap0 f  Rhat n.eff
# mean.sjuv 0.334 0.168 0.122 0.292  0.764    FALSE 1 1.015   137
# mean.sad  0.604 0.215 0.232 0.607  0.976    FALSE 1 1.015   134
# mean.p    0.502 0.204 0.200 0.456  0.930    FALSE 1 1.016   118
# deviance  9.974 2.009 8.005 9.329 15.306    FALSE 1 1.014   279



library(R2WinBUGS)
ipm <- bugs(jags.data, inits, parameters, "ipmn.jags", n.chains = 3, n.thin = 6, n.iter = 2000, n.burnin = 500, debug = F)
print(ipm, digits = 3)
# Inference for Bugs model at "ipmn.jags", fit using WinBUGS,
# 3 chains, each with 2000 iterations (first 500 discarded), n.thin = 6
# n.sims = 750 iterations saved
# mean    sd    2.5%     25%     50%     75%   97.5%  Rhat n.eff
# mean.sjuv   0.269 0.024   0.227   0.251   0.268   0.285   0.321 0.999   750
# mean.sad    0.526 0.030   0.467   0.505   0.526   0.547   0.585 1.016   130
# mean.p      0.610 0.040   0.529   0.584   0.611   0.637   0.688 0.999   750
# deviance  197.661 2.387 194.900 196.000 197.000 198.800 203.927 1.000   750
#
# For each parameter, n.eff is a crude measure of effective sample size,
# and Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor (at convergence, Rhat=1).
#
# DIC info (using the rule, pD = Dbar-Dhat)
# pD = 3.0 and DIC = 200.6
# DIC is an estimate of expected predictive error (lower deviance is better).



library(nimble)
codejags<-readBUGSmodel('ipmn.jags',data=jags.data,inits=inits)
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(codejags)
Cmodel <- compileNimble(codejags)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = codejags)
Cmcmc$run(10000)
samples <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)[2000:10000,]
apply(samples, 2, mean)
# mean.p  mean.sad mean.sjuv
# 0.6078309 0.5273773 0.2692511
apply(samples, 2, sd)
# mean.p   mean.sad  mean.sjuv
# 0.03982141 0.02839809 0.02488084

parts:
Without looking closely at your code, one of the first places I might look when troubleshooting is the initial values. I know that JAGS has different requirements for initial values than WinBUGS, at least for occupancy models and N-mixture models. Sometimes they can have a big influence on how well the model performs.

 

Andrew D. Crosby
Postdoctoral Fellow
Boreal Avian Modelling Project
751 General Services Building
University of Alberta
Edmonton, AB T6G 2H1

Without looking closely at your code, one of the first places I might look when troubleshooting is the initial values. I know that JAGS has different requirements for initial values than WinBUGS, at least for occupancy models and N-mixture models. Sometimes they can have a big influence on how well the model performs.

From: Floriane Plard
Sent: Monday, October 1, 2018 10:27 AM
To: hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology
Subject: Inconsistent mean and sd in CMR models from JAGS compared to winbugsand nimble

 


I compared the results of a simple Capture-mark-recapture model using an m-array from Jags, Winbugs and nimble.
Surprisingly, Jags gave different mean results and wider sd than nimble and Winbugs which gave similar results.
The 95% credible interval sin JAGS are thus very large. For instance for the probability of recapture:

  jags gave 0.20-0.93 compared to the others program: 0.53-0.64. The conclusions from JAGS can thus be really different form the other program.

Would anyone have an idea about the causes of these differences?

  Thanks
Floriane

Reproducible example:


# Capture-recapture data (in m-array format, from years 1 to 10)
m <- matrix(c(11,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  70,
              0, 12,  0,  1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  52,
              0,  0, 15,  5,  1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  42,
              0,  0,  0,  8,  3,  0,  0,  0,  0,  51,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  4,  3,  0,  0,  0,  61,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 12,  2,  3,  0,  66,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 16,  5,  0,  44,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 12,  0,  46,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 11,  71,
              10,  2,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  13,
              0,  7,  0,  1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  27,
              0,  0, 13,  2,  1,  1,  0,  0,  0,  14,
              0,  0,  0, 12,  2,  0,  0,  0,  0,  20,
              0,  0,  0,  0, 10,  2,  0,  0,  0,  21,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 11,  2,  1,  1,  14,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 12,  0,  0,  18,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 11,  1,  21,
              0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, 10,  26), ncol = 10, byrow = TRUE)


sink("ipmn.jags")
cat("
    model {
    # Survival and recapture probabilities, as well as productivity
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    sjuv[t] <- mean.sjuv
    sad[t] <- mean.sad
    p[t] <- mean.p
    }
   
    mean.sjuv ~ dunif(0, 1)
    mean.sad ~ dunif(0, 1)
    mean.p ~ dunif(0, 1)
   
    # 3.2 Likelihood for capture-recapture data: CJS model (2 age classes)
    # Multinomial likelihood
    for (t in 1:2*(nyears-1)){
    m[t,1:nyears] ~ dmulti(pr[t,1:nyears], r[t])
    }
   
    # m-array cell probabilities for juveniles
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    # Main diagonal
    q[t] <- 1-p[t]
    pr[t,t] <- sjuv[t] * p[t]
    # Above main diagonal
    for (j in (t+1):(nyears-1)){
    pr[t,j] <- sjuv[t]*prod(sad[(t+1):j])*prod(q[t:(j-1)])*p[j]
    } #j   
    # Below main diagonal
    for (j in 1:(t-1)){
    pr[t,j] <- 0
    } #j
    # Last column: probability of non-recapture
    pr[t,nyears] <- 1-sum(pr[t,1:(nyears-1)])
    } #t
   
    # m-array cell probabilities for adults
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    # Main diagonal
    pr[t+nyears-1,t] <- sad[t] * p[t]
    # Above main diagonal
    for (j in (t+1):(nyears-1)){
    pr[t+nyears-1,j] <- prod(sad[t:j])*prod(q[t:(j-1)])*p[j]
    } #j
    # Below main diagonal
    for (j in 1:(t-1)){
    pr[t+nyears-1,j] <- 0
    } #j
    # Last column
    pr[t+nyears-1,nyears] <- 1 - sum(pr[t+nyears-1,1:(nyears-1)])
    } #t
   
    }
    ",fill = TRUE)
sink()

jags.data <- list(m = m, nyears = dim(m)[2], r = rowSums(m))
inits <- list(mean.sjuv = 0.5, mean.sad = 0.5, mean.p = 0.5)
parameters <- c("mean.sjuv", "mean.sad", "mean.p")
library(jagsUI)
ipm <- jags(jags.data, inits, parameters, "ipmn.jags", n.chains = 3, n.thin = 6, n.iter = 2000, n.burnin = 500)
print(ipm, digits = 3)
# mean    sd  2.5%   50%  97.5% overlap0 f  Rhat n.eff
# mean.sjuv 0.334 0.168 0.122 0.292  0.764    FALSE 1 1.015   137
# mean.sad  0.604 0.215 0.232 0.607  0.976    FALSE 1 1.015   134
# mean.p    0.502 0.204 0.200 0.456  0.930    FALSE 1 1.016   118
# deviance  9.974 2.009 8.005 9.329 15.306    FALSE 1 1.014   279



library(R2WinBUGS)
ipm <- bugs(jags.data, inits, parameters, "ipmn.jags", n.chains = 3, n.thin = 6, n.iter = 2000, n.burnin = 500, debug = F)
print(ipm, digits = 3)
# Inference for Bugs model at "ipmn.jags", fit using WinBUGS,
# 3 chains, each with 2000 iterations (first 500 discarded), n.thin = 6
# n.sims = 750 iterations saved
# mean    sd    2.5%     25%     50%     75%   97.5%  Rhat n.eff
# mean.sjuv   0.269 0.024   0.227   0.251   0.268   0.285   0.321 0.999   750
# mean.sad    0.526 0.030   0.467   0.505   0.526   0.547   0.585 1.016   130
# mean.p      0.610 0.040   0.529   0.584   0.611   0.637   0.688 0.999   750
# deviance  197.661 2.387 194.900 196.000 197.000 198.800 203.927 1.000   750
#
# For each parameter, n.eff is a crude measure of effective sample size,
# and Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor (at convergence, Rhat=1).
#
# DIC info (using the rule, pD = Dbar-Dhat)
# pD = 3.0 and DIC = 200.6
# DIC is an estimate of expected predictive error (lower deviance is better).



library(nimble)
codejags<-readBUGSmodel('ipmn.jags',data=jags.data,inits=inits)
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(codejags)
Cmodel <- compileNimble(codejags)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = codejags)
Cmcmc$run(10000)
samples <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)[2000:10000,]
apply(samples, 2, mean)
# mean.p  mean.sad mean.sjuv
# 0.6078309 0.5273773 0.2692511
apply(samples, 2, sd)
# mean.p   mean.sad  mean.sjuv
# 0.03982141 0.02839809 0.02488084
